runs.answer: No — Lamar Jackson is not playing. Head Coach Jesse Minter ruled him out Friday (Oct 16, 2026) with the ankle injury he suffered in the Week 4 win over the Titans; he has not practiced since (12 days, no practice all week) and this is his second straight missed game. Tyler "Snoop" Huntley starts again at quarterback after leading the comeback 30-23 overtime win in Atlanta. runs.title: 737 MAX 10: has the FAA approved it?
runs.prompt: Boeing's long-delayed 737 MAX 10 is reportedly close to FAA certification. Visit https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/faa-set-approve-737-max-10-soon-next-week-2026-10-16/ and https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-10-16/faa-set-to-approve-737-max-10-as-soon-as-next-week . Report: has the FAA formally approved the 737 MAX 10 yet? What is the expected timing, and what do the FAA or Boeing say about any remaining steps?
runs.answer: No — as of the latest reporting (Oct 17, 2026), the FAA has not yet formally issued the 737 MAX 10 type certificate. Boeing and the FAA held a successful Type Certification Board meeting on Friday, Oct. 16, which cleared the final formal review; Boeing must now submit a Project Statement of Completion (PSOC), after which the FAA is expected to sign the amended type certificate as soon as the week of Oct. 19 (the MAX 7 followed the same pattern: Friday board meeting, certificate signed the following week). The remaining wrinkle is flight-management software (FMC U14/U14.1) whose go-around/VNAV behavior the FAA judged not a safety issue and does not require fixing before certification — it issued only a non-mandatory bulletin — but United, Alaska, American and Southwest say they will not take MAX 10s fitted with that software; Boeing says it is pulling forward a permanent software fix (originally 2028) and new pilot guidance (due November) and is working with airlines on a re-engage-VNAV procedure. First deliveries, launch customer WestJet, are expected around spring 2027.
